blog_summary: Adrian Colyer summarizes key hardware trends in networking, memory, storage, and processing that are transforming data center design and distributed systems. He highlights the shift from 10GbE to 40GbE/100GbE/400GbE Ethernet, enabling ultra-low latency (down to ~2.4µs round-trip) with technologies like RDMA (Remote Direct Memory Access) and RoCE (RDMA over Converged Ethernet), which can achieve ~1.4µs latency by bypassing the CPU. The blog also discusses NVRAM (Non-volatile RAM) technologies like 3D XPoint, which blur the lines between memory and storage, offering persistent memory with higher capacity and lower cost than DRAM. Storage advancements like NVMe and PCIe 4.0 further enhance performance, while new processing technologies such as FPGAs, hardware transactional memory (HTM), and persistent memory support are improving energy efficiency and reducing latency in data centers.
